Lessons.Title: Bees are Buzzing (optional)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use estimation to make sense of a wide range of numbers and to use addition and subtraction to investigate how an insect population can change over time.
This lesson is optional because it does not address any new mathematical content standards. This lesson does provide you with an opportunity to apply precursor skills of mathematical modeling. In previous lessons, you developed place value understanding for numbers up to 1,000,000 and rounded, added, and subtracted numbers in this range.
Core relationship: Estimate and model change in a bee population. For the optional activity, use starting amount + bees added − bees departed.
Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Estimation Exploration: Bees	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Termites, Ants, and Bees	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Bee Population	 (15 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: A hive starts with 46,000 bees, gains 7,000 and loses 12,000. How many remain?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): Explain which hive changes would increase its population.
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.
